environment.description: Agent News is a research and verification service for the AI-agent economy. It aggregates structured news events, articles, product and action metadata, and externally researched evidence to answer questions and produce sourced recommendations about AI agents, tools, MCP servers, and frameworks. The workflow emphasizes citation-backed claims, confidence and relevance diagnostics, ethics ratings, provenance verification, editorial standards, and explicit insufficient-evidence responses. It also supports article discovery, topic hubs, trust metrics, threaded comments, and optional usage reporting.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_search
init_ref_tools.description: Search The Agent Times agent-news layer across structured events, articles, and agent-action/product metadata. Uses backend typo correction, alias expansion, required-term coverage, global ranking, and low-confidence rejection. Returns search_confidence, warnings, relevance_score, match_quality, matched_terms, missing_terms, sources, confidence, Ethics Engine score, agent voice score, and standard receipt.

query.description: Short entity-rich English search query for agent-news, articles, products, actions, or events

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_ask
init_ref_tools.description: Ask The Agent Times a question through the trusted answer pipeline: TAT corpus/events/action metadata plus backend-controlled external research, with citations, confidence, Ethics Engine score, agent voice score, and answer-standard receipt. Returns insufficient_evidence instead of unsourced claims. Set instant_answer=true to force a synchronous, fully-processed answer (used by the on-site Ask Expert widget).

question.description: English question to answer using TAT corpus/events/action metadata plus backend-controlled verified external research

instant_answer.description: When true, answer synchronously through the full TAT answer pipeline and never return a processing/deferral response. Omit or set false to keep the fast cached/local path that may defer with status='processing'.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_get_event
init_ref_tools.description: Fetch one structured agent-news event by event_id, including sources, confidence, ethics score, agent voice score, recommended actions, and standard receipt.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_stats
init_ref_tools.description: Return firehose/demo counters for recent agent-news events: counts, verification rate, average confidence, source count, urgency, and actionability breakdowns.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_get_answer_standard
init_ref_tools.description: Return the current The Agent Times MCP Answer Standard so agents can explain why a TAT answer/event is trusted, or why insufficient_evidence was returned.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_recommend
init_ref_tools.description: Return sourced recommendations for an agent/operator use case using TAT trusted corpus, events, and answer standard. Not an external-resource safety checker.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_get_comments
init_ref_tools.description: Read threaded comments on a TAT article, with agent attribution and endorsement counts.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: tat_post_comment
init_ref_tools.description: Post a signed/logged agent comment on a TAT article. Use only when the user explicitly asks to post.

model.description: Your model identifier

operator.description: Operator/organization

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_latest_articles
init_ref_tools.description: Get the latest articles from The Agent Times. Returns headlines, summaries, sources, confidence levels, and Ed25519 provenance status.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_section_articles
init_ref_tools.description: Get articles from a specific section. Each article includes Ed25519 provenance status. Sections: platforms, open-source, research, commerce, sales, marketing, engineering, adtech, infrastructure, regulations, funding, labor, opinion, interview.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_article
init_ref_tools.description: Get a full article by slug, including the complete body text and Ed25519 provenance verification status. Optionally include detailed provenance and governance blocks.

slug.description: Article slug (from the URL)

include_governance.description: Include the detailed content governance block and usage terms when the user asks what agents may do with the article

include_provenance.description: Include the detailed Ed25519 provenance receipt when the user asks how authorship is verified

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: search_articles
init_ref_tools.description: Search The Agent Times article corpus with typo-tolerant required-term coverage, relevance diagnostics, and filters over title, slug, tags, summary, body, and publication metadata. Returns the same structured contract as tat_search (search_confidence, warnings, relevance diagnostics, sources, confidence, Ethics Engine score, agent voice score, and standard receipt) restricted to article results.

query.description: Search query

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_related_articles
init_ref_tools.description: Get related articles for an article slug using section/topic/tag overlap.

slug.description: Article slug

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: list_topics
init_ref_tools.description: List known topic hubs extracted from the corpus.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_topic_hub
init_ref_tools.description: Get a topic hub with start-here articles, latest coverage, and intent tags.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_trust_summary
init_ref_tools.description: Get publication-level trust metrics: confidence mix, provenance coverage, source density, and section-level trust summaries.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: get_editorial_standards
init_ref_tools.description: Get The Agent Times editorial standards and code of conduct summary.

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

init_ref_tools.name: report_usage
init_ref_tools.description: Voluntarily declare which TAT articles you used to produce your output. Transparent agents build trust and get recognized as verified consumers. No auth required — just tell us what you used.

article_slugs.description: List of article slugs you used (from the URL)

output_description.description: Brief description of what you produced using these articles

text.description: Present when the tool returns a text-only response.

data_directions: Official product documentation, release notes, changelogs, and vendor announcements for AI-agent platforms, tools, MCP servers, and frameworks
Open-source repositories, commit histories, issue trackers, package registries, licenses, and security advisories
Research papers, preprints, benchmarks, model cards, datasets, and institutional lab publications
Technology-news articles, interviews, opinion pieces, newsletters, and trade-publication coverage
Company websites, press releases, funding announcements, investor disclosures, and acquisition records
Public pricing pages, product catalogs, integration directories, API references, and marketplace listings
Government regulations, legislative proposals, regulator guidance, enforcement actions, and public-policy consultations
Infrastructure status pages, incident reports, vulnerability databases, and reliability disclosures
Public labor-market data, job postings, workforce reports, and studies of automation's employment effects
Public commerce, sales, marketing, advertising-technology, and engineering case studies involving AI agents
Cryptographically signed publication records, timestamps, authorship metadata, source links, and other provenance evidence
Public discussion threads, article comments, endorsements, and attributed expert or agent commentary
Editorial policies, codes of conduct, correction records, trust reports, and source-quality methodologies

environment.description: OneSignal is a multichannel customer engagement platform for creating, targeting, sending, and measuring push notifications, email, SMS, in-app messages, and iOS Live Activities. It supports audience segmentation, user identities and subscriptions, reusable templates, custom-event-driven journeys, campaign analytics, and subscription lifecycle management.

init_ref_tools.name: create_alias_by_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Create or update identity aliases for the user who owns a given subscription. The `onesignal_id` alias is read-only and must not be included.

aliases.description: New aliases to set on the user. Do not include `onesignal_id` (read-only).

subscription_id.description: Subscription ID to look up the user by.

init_ref_tools.name: create_custom_events
init_ref_tools.description: Record custom events for OneSignal users, such as purchases, content views, or milestones. Use these to enter users into Journeys or trigger Wait Until nodes. Each event must set at least one of `external_id` or `onesignal_id`.

events.description:
Array of event objects to record. Each event must have `name` and
either `external_id` or `onesignal_id` set.

init_ref_tools.name: create_or_update_alias
init_ref_tools.description: Create or update identity aliases for a user identified by alias. The `onesignal_id` alias is read-only and must not be included.

aliases.description: New aliases to set on the user. Do not include `onesignal_id` (read-only).

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

init_ref_tools.name: create_segment
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new audience segment with filter conditions. Maximum 200 filter entries.

filters.description: Segment filter conditions. Maximum 200 entries.

init_ref_tools.name: create_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new subscription and attach it to a user. Set `type` to the channel ("Email", "SMS", "iOSPush", "AndroidPush", etc.) and `token` to the email address, E.164 phone number, or push token.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

init_ref_tools.name: create_template
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new notification template for a OneSignal app.

extra.description:
Additional notification fields. Common keys: `big_picture`, `chrome_web_image`,
`ios_sound`, `android_sound`, `ios_badge_type`, `ios_badge_count`,
`data` (custom key-value payload), `url`, `web_url`, `app_url`,
`buttons`, `web_buttons`, `ios_category`, `android_channel_id`.

contents.description: Notification content map (language code → message). E.g. `{"en": "Hello!"}`.

email_body.description:
HTML body for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

email_subject.description:
Subject line for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

init_ref_tools.name: create_user
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new user in a OneSignal app. Provide an `identity` (e.g. {"external_id": "user-123"}) so the user can be referenced later by alias. Optionally attach `properties` (tags, language, country) and `subscriptions` (email, SMS, or push channels). The `identity` field is required to prevent orphaned users.

identity.description:
User identity aliases (e.g. `{"external_id": "user-123"}`).
Required — without an identity the user cannot be referenced later
by alias, resulting in orphaned records.

ip.description: User's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Typically set by the API response; rarely set manually.

tags.description:
Custom key-value pairs for user segmentation and personalization.
Keys and values must be strings. Does not support nested objects or arrays.
Example: `{"plan": "premium", "level": "5"}`.

country.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format (uppercase). Example: `"US"`, `"GB"`.

language.description: Language code in ISO 639-1 format (lowercase). Example: `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`.

last_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the user's most recent activity.

timezone_id.description: Timezone identifier from the IANA tz database. Example: `"America/Los_Angeles"`.

first_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the user was first active.

properties.description: User profile properties (tags, language, country, location, etc.).

subscriptions.description: Subscriptions to attach to this user (push, email, or SMS channels).

init_ref_tools.name: export_audience_activity_csv
init_ref_tools.description: Export audience activity for a notification to CSV. WARNING: Only 1 concurrent export is allowed per account — if a 409 or 429 is returned, a previous export is still running.

email.description: Email address to deliver the report to. Optional.

events.description:
Type of events to retrieve. `"sent"` — users the notification was sent to;
`"clicked"` — users who clicked the notification.

notification_id.description: Notification ID to export audience activity for.

init_ref_tools.name: export_subscriptions_csv
init_ref_tools.description: Export all subscriptions for a OneSignal app to CSV. WARNING: Only 1 concurrent export is allowed per account — if a 409 or 429 is returned, a previous export is still running.

extra_fields.description: Optional list of extra fields to include in the export.

segment_name.description: Optional segment name to filter subscriptions by.

last_active_since.description: Unix timestamp (seconds). Only include subscriptions active since this time.

init_ref_tools.name: get_custom_events
init_ref_tools.description: List the custom event definitions indexed for a OneSignal app, including each event's properties, sources, most recent occurrence, usage locations (segment/journey), storage and total counts, and retention duration. Requires OAuth authentication.

init_ref_tools.name: get_segment
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a single audience segment by ID. By default, includes full segment metadata and filters (`payload` object with `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `source`, and `filters`). Set `include_segment_detail` to `false` to return only the subscriber count. Note: the API returns 400 for user-based segments (those using custom_event or message_event filters).

include_segment_detail.description:
If `true` (default), includes segment metadata and filters in the
response (`payload` object with `id`, `name`, `created_at`, `source`,
and `filters`). Set to `false` to return only the subscriber count.

init_ref_tools.name: get_template
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a single notification template by ID.

init_ref_tools.name: get_user_identity
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve all identity aliases associated with a user. Identify the user by `alias_label` (typically "external_id") and `alias_id`.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to look up the user. Typically `"external_id"`.

init_ref_tools.name: get_user_identity_by_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve the identity aliases for the user who owns a given subscription.

init_ref_tools.name: list_apps
init_ref_tools.description: List OneSignal apps accessible to the authenticated user. Returns app names, IDs, and organization info. Supports pagination via limit and offset parameters.

limit.description: Maximum number of apps to return. Defaults to 50; maximum allowed is 300.

offset.description: Pagination offset.

init_ref_tools.name: list_messages
init_ref_tools.description: List push notifications for a OneSignal app. Use `limit` (default 50, max ~250) and `offset` for pagination. Avoid large offsets — this endpoint has known performance degradation at high page numbers.

kind.description: Filter by how the notification was created: `0` = Dashboard, `1` = API, `3` = Automated.

limit.description: Maximum number of notifications to return. Defaults to 50. Max ~250.

offset.description: Pagination offset.

time_offset.description: ISO 8601 timestamp or Base64 integer token for cursor-based pagination (from previous response).

init_ref_tools.name: list_segments
init_ref_tools.description: List audience segments for a OneSignal app. Maximum 300 segments per page.

limit.description: Maximum number of segments to return per page. Maximum 300.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Maximum 300 segments per page.

init_ref_tools.name: list_templates
init_ref_tools.description: List notification templates for a OneSignal app. Maximum 50 per page.

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Max 50 per page.

offset.description: Pagination offset.

init_ref_tools.name: onesignal_config
init_ref_tools.description: Return the current OneSignal MCP server configuration and connected app details.

init_ref_tools.name: onesignal_health
init_ref_tools.description: Check the health status of the OneSignal MCP server.

init_ref_tools.name: onesignal_reference_overview
init_ref_tools.description: Return an overview of the OneSignal REST API reference, including available endpoints and rate limits.

init_ref_tools.name: send_message
init_ref_tools.description: Send a push notification, email, or SMS via the OneSignal API. TIER 3 — HIGH IMPACT: confirmation is required before sending. Rate limited to 10 requests per minute. The `filters` array is limited to 200 entries; max 20,000 users per call. For push: set `contents`. For email: set `email_subject` + `email_body` (or use `template_id`). For SMS: set `contents` + `target_channel = "sms"`.

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds. Notification expires if not delivered within this window. Push only.

url.description: URL to open when the push notification is clicked.

data.description: Custom data payload passed through to the app (key-value map). Push only.

name.description: An internal name to help organize messages. Not shown to recipients. Max 128 chars.

filters.description: Audience filters. Maximum 200 entries. Mutually exclusive with `included_segments`.

contents.description:
Notification content map (language code → message). E.g. `{"en": "Hello!"}`.
Required for push and SMS. Not required for email (use `email_body` instead).

email_to.description:
Send email to specific addresses (up to 20,000). Creates new subscriptions if needed.
Mutually exclusive with `filters`, `included_segments`, `include_aliases`.

headings.description: Notification heading map (language code → heading). Push only.

sms_from.description: The phone number or messaging service used to send SMS/MMS. Defaults to your SMS Setup.

email_bcc.description:
BCC recipients to copy on the email. Supplemental to the primary recipients
(`email_to`, segments, aliases) — does not target on its own.

email_body.description: HTML body for email messages. Required for email unless using `template_id`.

send_after.description:
Schedule delivery for a future UTC date/time in ISO 8601 format.
Example: `"2025-09-24T14:00:00-07:00"`.

custom_data.description:
Custom data payload for push notifications, or personalization data for templates.
Max size: 2KB (push/SMS), 10KB (email).

template_id.description: Template ID (UUID v4) to use for message content.

email_subject.description: Subject line for email messages. Required for email unless using `template_id`.

sms_media_urls.description: URLs of media files to send as MMS. Requires MMS-capable `sms_from` number.

target_channel.description:
The delivery channel when using `include_aliases` or segments for SMS.
Accepts `"push"`, `"email"`, or `"sms"`.

email_from_name.description: The sender display name for the email. Defaults to your Dashboard "Sender Name".

email_preheader.description: Preview text displayed after the email subject line in the inbox.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key (UUID) to prevent duplicate messages. Valid for 30 days.

include_aliases.description:
Target users by alias (e.g. `{"external_id": ["user_1"]}`). Up to 20,000 aliases.
Requires `target_channel` to be set. Mutually exclusive with `filters`, `included_segments`.

excluded_segments.description: Exclude segments by name. Use with `included_segments`.

included_segments.description: Target segments by name. Mutually exclusive with `filters` and `include_aliases`.

email_from_address.description: The "From" email address (e.g. `"news@example.com"`). Defaults to your Dashboard setting.

email_sender_domain.description: The authenticated sending domain for email delivery. Must be verified in DNS.

delivery_time_of_day.description:
Use with `delayed_option: "timezone"` to set local delivery time.
Formats: `"9:00AM"`, `"21:45"`, `"09:45:30"`.

include_unsubscribed.description: If `true`, sends email to unsubscribed addresses. Use for transactional/account emails only.

include_phone_numbers.description:
Send SMS to specific phone numbers in E.164 format (up to 20,000).
Creates new subscriptions if needed. Mutually exclusive with other targeting.

email_reply_to_address.description: The "Reply-To" email address. Defaults to your Dashboard setting.

include_subscription_ids.description:
Specific subscription IDs to target (up to 20,000). IMPORTANT: You must also
set `target_channel` to `"email"` or `"sms"` when targeting email or SMS subscriptions,
otherwise the API will reject them as invalid push IDs.

disable_email_click_tracking.description: If `true`, disables click tracking on URLs in the email body.

init_ref_tools.name: start_live_activity
init_ref_tools.description: Start an iOS Live Activity and deliver it to a specific device subscription.

name.description: An internal name to help organize and track messages.

event.description: The action to perform. Must be `"start"` for this endpoint.

filters.description: Dynamic audience filters.

contents.description: Push message body with language-specific values. E.g. `{"en": "Game started!"}`.

headings.description: Push title with language-specific values. E.g. `{"en": "Live Score"}`.

stale_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the Live Activity is considered stale.

activity_id.description: An identifier you set when starting the Live Activity to uniquely identify it on the device.

activity_type.description: Activity type identifier used in the URL path (e.g. `"sports-score"`).

event_updates.description: Initial dynamic content state for the Live Activity.

idempotency_key.description: Idempotency key to prevent duplicate messages.

include_aliases.description: Target users by alias map (e.g. `{"external_id": ["user1", "user2"]}`). Max 20,000.

event_attributes.description: Static data to initialize the Live Activity (matches your ActivityAttributes struct).

ios_relevance_score.description: Relevance score between `0` and `1` for sorting Live Activities (iOS).

init_ref_tools.name: transfer_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Transfer a subscription to a different user within the same app. Cross-app transfers are not supported. Rate limited to 1 request per second per subscription.

identity.description: Identity of the user to transfer the subscription to.

init_ref_tools.name: unsubscribe_email
init_ref_tools.description: Unsubscribe an email address using the token from an email unsubscribe link. This endpoint uses token-based auth (no REST API key required).

token.description: Unsubscribe token from the email link.

notification_id.description: Notification ID from the unsubscribe link.

init_ref_tools.name: update_live_activity
init_ref_tools.description: Update or end an active iOS Live Activity.

name.description: An internal name to help organize and track messages.

event.description: The action to perform on the Live Activity. `"update"` or `"end"`.

contents.description: Optional push message body shown alongside the Live Activity update.

stale_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) after which the Live Activity is considered stale.

event_updates.description: Updated dynamic content state for the Live Activity.

dismissal_date.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) indicating when the Live Activity should be dismissed.

ios_relevance_score.description: Relevance score between `0` and `1` for sorting Live Activities (iOS).

init_ref_tools.name: update_segment
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing audience segment's name and/or filter conditions. `name` is always required even if not changing it (max 128 characters). When `filters` is provided it replaces all existing filters; omit to keep existing filters intact. Maximum 200 filter entries.

name.description:
Segment name. Required — must be provided even if not changing it.
Maximum 128 characters.

filters.description:
Updated filter conditions. Maximum 200 entries. When provided, replaces
all existing filters. Omit to keep existing filters intact.

init_ref_tools.name: update_subscription
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing subscription (token, enabled status, or test type).

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

init_ref_tools.name: update_subscription_by_token
init_ref_tools.description: Update a subscription identified by its channel type and token. Provide `subscription_type` and `token` to identify the subscription, then pass the fields to update in `subscription`.

token.description: The push token, email address, or phone number for this subscription.

enabled.description: Whether this subscription is enabled (i.e. can receive notifications).

subscription_type.description:
Subscription type segment in the URL path. Must match the subscription
channel type exactly (e.g. `"Email"`, `"SMS"`, `"AndroidPush"`, `"iOSPush"`).

init_ref_tools.name: update_template
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing notification template. The `name` field is required even if you are not changing it.

name.description: Template name. Required even if unchanged.

extra.description:
Additional notification fields to update. Common keys: `big_picture`, `chrome_web_image`,
`ios_sound`, `android_sound`, `ios_badge_type`, `ios_badge_count`,
`data` (custom key-value payload), `url`, `web_url`, `app_url`,
`buttons`, `web_buttons`, `ios_category`, `android_channel_id`.

email_body.description:
HTML body for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

email_subject.description:
Subject line for email templates. When provided, the template is automatically
marked as an email template (`isEmail: true`).

init_ref_tools.name: update_user
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing user identified by alias. Use `properties` to set tags, language, or country. Use `deltas` to increment session counts or append purchase records (these add to existing values rather than overwriting). Returns 202 — the update is processed asynchronously.

purchases.description: Purchase records to append to the user's purchase history.

session_time.description: Seconds to add to the user's total session time.

session_count.description: Number of sessions to add to the user's session count.

deltas.description:
Incremental deltas to apply to session/purchase stats.
Supported keys: `session_count` (integer), `session_time` (integer seconds),
`purchases` (array of purchase objects with `sku`, `iso`, `amount`).

ip.description: User's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Typically set by the API response; rarely set manually.

tags.description:
Custom key-value pairs for user segmentation and personalization.
Keys and values must be strings. Does not support nested objects or arrays.
Example: `{"plan": "premium", "level": "5"}`.

country.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 format (uppercase). Example: `"US"`, `"GB"`.

language.description: Language code in ISO 639-1 format (lowercase). Example: `"en"`, `"es"`, `"fr"`.

last_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the user's most recent activity.

timezone_id.description: Timezone identifier from the IANA tz database. Example: `"America/Los_Angeles"`.

first_active.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of when the user was first active.

properties.description: User profile properties to update (tags, language, country, location, etc.).

alias_label.description: Alias label used to identify the user (e.g. `"external_id"`).

refresh_device_metadata.description: If `true`, refreshes device metadata (timezone, locale, etc.) from the subscription.

init_ref_tools.name: view_message
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a single notification by ID.

outcome_names.description:
Outcome names to retrieve for this message, with aggregation type.

Examples:
- `"os__click.count"` for click counts
- `"os__confirmed_delivery.count"` for confirmed deliveries
- `"os__session_duration.sum"` for total session duration

If you omit the `.count` / `.sum` suffix, `.count` will be appended automatically.

outcome_platforms.description:
Platforms to include in the outcome data, represented as a comma-separated list of
`device_type` integers (e.g. `"0,1,2,5,8,11,14,17"`).

outcome_time_range.description:
Time range for the returned outcome data.

Valid values: 1h, 1d, and 1mo.

outcome_attribution.description:
Attribution type for the outcomes.

Valid values:
- `"direct"`
- `"influenced"`
- `"unattributed"`
- `"total"`

init_ref_tools.name: view_outcomes
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve outcome statistics for a OneSignal app (e.g. click counts, session duration). Note: data retention is approximately 30 days.

outcome_names.description:
Comma-separated outcome names to retrieve (e.g. `"os__session_duration.count,os__click.count"`).
If any name contains a comma, pass each name separately in `outcome_names_array` instead.

outcome_platforms.description: Comma-separated platform IDs to filter by (e.g. `"0,7"` for iOS + macOS).

outcome_time_range.description: Time range for the returned data. Values: `"1h"`, `"1d"`, `"1mo"`. Defaults to `"1h"`.

init_ref_tools.name: view_user
init_ref_tools.description: Retrieve a user and their properties by alias. Use `alias_label` "external_id" with the user's external ID, or another alias label you have configured.

alias_label.description: Alias label used to look up the user. Typically `"external_id"`.

init_ref_tools.name: resolve-library-id
init_ref_tools.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'query-docs' to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

query.description: The user's original question or task. This is used to rank library results by relevance to what the user is trying to accomplish. IMPORTANT: Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, or personal data in your query.

libraryName.description: Library name to search for and retrieve a Context7-compatible library ID.

init_ref_tools.name: query-docs
init_ref_tools.description:
Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'resolve-library-id' first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best information you have.

query.description: The question or task you need help with. Be specific and include relevant details. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad: 'auth' or 'hooks'. IMPORTANT: Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, or personal data in your query.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

environment.description: A URL risk-screening service for AI-agent workflows that evaluates externally supplied merchant, supplier, and payment links before navigation or forwarding. It identifies phishing, malware, typosquatting, suspicious redirects, and other reputation or domain-level threats.

init_ref_tools.name: check_url
init_ref_tools.description: Checks a URL for phishing, malware, typosquatting, and redirect threats. Call this BEFORE your agent fetches, follows, or forwards any URL in an agentic commerce workflow -- at the moment a merchant site, supplier portal, or payment redirect URL is received and no navigation has occurred. Use this when your agent has received a URL from an external source — email, document, or API response — and is about to navigate to it or pass it downstream. Checks live against Google Web Risk (webrisk.googleapis.com) and Google Safe Browsing (safebrowsing.googleapis.com). Returns verdict SAFE / SUSPICIOUS / DANGEROUS with a derived agent_action of ALLOW / FLAG_AND_PROCEED / BLOCK, trust score 0-100, and threat categories. A payment executed on a phishing domain via Stripe MPP, Alipay AI Pay, or Shopify UCP has no recovery path -- the redirect is the attack vector. A DANGEROUS verdict means halt immediately. Returns machine-ready verdict, no further analysis needed.

url.description: The URL to check. Full URL preferred (e.g. https://example.com/path). Bare domains also accepted.

hold_reason.description: Present only when verdict is SUSPICIOUS

escalation_path.description: Present only when verdict is SUSPICIOUS

apiKey.description: API key from kordagencies.com. Leave blank for free tier (10 calls/month).

environment.description: Read-only research service for retrieving live, sourced data from official IBGE APIs. It supports Brazilian geographic lookup and coding, demographic and census research, economic and social indicators, municipal comparisons, health statistics, survey discovery, release tracking, and map acquisition. A typical workflow is to identify a locality or survey, inspect available tables and metadata, query exact figures, and retain IBGE provenance.

init_ref_tools.name: ibge_estados
init_ref_tools.description:
Lists all Brazilian states from IBGE.

Features:
- Lists all 27 states (26 states + Federal District)
- Filter by region (North, Northeast, Southeast, South, Central-West)
- Sort by ID, name, or abbreviation

Examples:
- List all states: (no parameters)
- Northeast states: regiao="NE"
- Sorted by abbreviation: ordenar="sigla"

Use a different tool when:
- Municipalities of a state → ibge_municipios
- Details/hierarchy of one locality by code → ibge_localidade

Behavior: read-only and idempotent — a live GET against the public IBGE Localidades API. Returns a Markdown table.

regiao.description: Filtrar por região: N (Norte), NE (Nordeste), SE (Sudeste), S (Sul), CO (Centro-Oeste)

total.description: Total de estados retornados

init_ref_tools.name: ibge_municipios
init_ref_tools.description:
Lists Brazilian municipalities from IBGE.

Features:
- List municipalities by state (using state abbreviation)
- List all municipalities in Brazil (5,570 municipalities)
- Search by municipality name
- Returns 7-digit IBGE code

Examples:
- São Paulo municipalities: uf="SP"
- Search by name: busca="Campinas"
- MG municipalities containing "Belo": uf="MG", busca="Belo"

Use a different tool when:
- Resolve/decode a code at any level (region, state, district), not just municipalities → ibge_geocodigo
- Full details/hierarchy of one locality by code → ibge_localidade
- Neighboring municipalities → ibge_vizinhos

Behavior: read-only and idempotent — a live GET against the public IBGE Localidades API. Returns a Markdown table.

uf.description: Estado por sigla (SP), nome (São Paulo) ou código IBGE (35). Se não informado, retorna todos os municípios do Brasil.

busca.description: Termo para buscar no nome do município

busca.description: Termo de busca aplicado ao nome do município

total.description: Total de municípios encontrados antes do limite

municipios.description: Lista de municípios retornados (após filtro e limite)

init_ref_tools.name: ibge_localidade
init_ref_tools.description:
Returns details of a specific locality by IBGE code.

Features:
- State information (2-digit code)
- Municipality information (7-digit code)
- District information (9-digit code)
- Complete hierarchy (region, mesoregion, microregion)

Examples:
- São Paulo state: codigo=35
- São Paulo city: codigo=3550308
- District: codigo=355030805

This tool returns the full record of ONE locality you already have the code for.
Use a different tool when:
- You have a name and need the code → ibge_municipios (municipalities) or ibge_geocodigo (any level)
- You want to decompose/understand a code's structure → ibge_geocodigo

Behavior: read-only and idempotent — a live GET against the public IBGE Localidades API. Returns a Markdown record.

tipo.description: Tipo da localidade. Se não informado, será inferido pelo tamanho do código.

codigo.description: Código IBGE da localidade (estado: 2 dígitos, município: 7 dígitos, distrito: 9 dígitos)

municipio.description: Município ao qual o distrito pertence (apenas para distritos)

init_ref_tools.description:
Returns real-time Brazilian population projection.

Features:
- Current population estimate
- Birth rate (average time between births)
- Death rate (average time between deaths)
- Daily population increment

Source: IBGE - Brazilian Population Projection

This tool ONLY returns Brazil's real-time national projection.

Use a different tool when:
- Population of a specific municipality/state → ibge_cidades (panorama)
- Census or historical population → ibge_censo
- Comparing/ranking multiple localities → ibge_comparar
- Population time series → ibge_indicadores
- An arbitrary SIDRA table → ibge_sidra

Behavior: read-only and idempotent — a live GET against the public IBGE population-projection API. Returns Markdown plus a typed structuredContent payload.

localidade.description: Localidade para projeção populacional (atualmente apenas BR disponível)

init_ref_tools.name: ibge_sidra
init_ref_tools.description:
Queries SIDRA tables (IBGE's Automatic Recovery System).

SIDRA contains data from IBGE surveys like Census, PNAD, GDP, etc.

Common tables:
- 6579: Population estimates (annual)
- 9514: Census 2022 population
- 200: Census population (1970-2010)
- 4714: Unemployment rate (PNAD Contínua)
- 6381: Average income (PNAD Contínua)
- 6706: GDP at current prices
- 5938: GDP per capita

Territorial levels:
- 1: Brazil
- 2: Region (North, Northeast, etc.)
- 3: State (UF)
- 6: Municipality
- 7: Metropolitan Region

Examples:
- Brazil population 2023: tabela="6579", periodos="2023"
- Population by state: tabela="6579", nivel_territorial="3"
- Census 2022 by municipality: tabela="9514", nivel_territorial="6", localidades="3550308"

ibge_sidra is the low-level engine. Prefer a friendlier wrapper when it fits:
- Census themes (1970–2022) → ibge_censo
- Economic/social time series → ibge_indicadores
- Rank/compare 2–10 localities → ibge_comparar
- One municipality's panel → ibge_cidades
Use ibge_sidra_tabelas and ibge_sidra_metadados to find a table code and its structure before querying.

Behavior: read-only and idempotent — a live GET against the public IBGE SIDRA API. Returns Markdown plus a typed structuredContent payload.

init_ref_tools.description:
Queries name frequency and rankings in Brazil (IBGE).

1. **Name frequency** (tipo='frequencia'):
   - Birth frequency by decade
   - Multiple names separated by comma
   - Filter by sex and locality

2. **Name ranking** (tipo='ranking'):

- Compare names: tipo="frequencia", nomes="João,José,Pedro"

init_ref_tools.name: ibge_noticias
init_ref_tools.description:
Searches and lists already-published IBGE news articles and press releases.

Use this to find recent IBGE publications or announcements about a survey or topic — when an indicator was released, or news mentioning a term like "censo". Results are sorted newest-first; with no parameters it returns the 10 most recent items.

Parameters:
- busca: free-text term to match (e.g. "PIB", "censo")
- tipo: "release" (official publication of survey results) or "noticia" (general news); omit for both
- de / ate: date range, format DD/MM/AAAA (e.g. de="01/01/2024", ate="31/12/2024")
- destaque: true to return only featured items
- quantidade: how many to return (default 10, max 100); pagina: page number to page through more

Each item returns: title, type (release/news), publication date, editoria (section), related products/surveys, a featured flag, a plain-text summary, and a link to the full article. The header reports the total count and current page.

Examples:
- Latest 10 news: (no parameters)
- Search census: busca="censo"
- 2024 news: de="01/01/2024", ate="31/12/2024"
- Releases only: tipo="release"

Use a different tool when:
- Scheduled/upcoming release dates (not yet published) → ibge_calendario
