data_directions: US listed-options chain data: OCC symbols, strikes, expirations, calls and puts, volume, open interest, bid/ask quotes, last trades, implied volatility, Greeks, and contract-level OHLCV
Unusual options activity and flow indicators: directional premium, sweep or block activity, volume-to-open-interest ratios, concentration, and overnight scanner scores
Underlying US equity market data: intraday and daily OHLCV, spot prices, returns, momentum, volatility, and technical trend indicators
Corporate-event calendars: scheduled earnings dates, earnings timing, dividends, splits, mergers, investor events, and other catalysts
Company and market news: press releases, SEC filings, financial-news headlines, analyst actions, and catalyst summaries with publication timestamps
Intraday option minute bars or trade tape for entry anchoring, first-crossing analysis, bracket replay, and MFE/MAE measurement
Historical option outcomes: realized premium returns, target and stop touches, time to peak or trough, holding-period labels, and liquidity-adjusted paper-trade results
Market-regime data: VIX, VIX3M, volatility-term-structure state, SPY trend measures, and recent volatility changes
NYSE market-calendar data: holidays, trading sessions, early closes, and next market open or close
Public methodology and documentation: signal-field definitions, leakage-safe data contracts, selection workflows, exit-rule playbooks, and methodology changelogs
Independent web sources for real-time news verification, company-specific catalyst research, and cross-checking market facts

environment.description: Wayforth is an API discovery, ranking, execution, and payment runtime for AI agents. It helps agents find services by intent or structured filters, compare providers, execute APIs through managed credentials or user-supplied keys, and pay through card credits or USDC/x402. The platform also offers service-health monitoring, reputation signals, usage analytics, and agent memory.

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_run
init_ref_tools.description:
The Wayforth runtime. One call does everything: searches for the best API,
    picks the top-ranked service by WayforthRank v2, maps your input to the
    service's params, and executes it — returning the result directly.

    Use this instead of wayforth_search + wayforth_execute when you just want the result.
    Supports: translation, weather, news, stock prices, web search, image generation,
    speech-to-text, text-to-speech, email, and 300+ more catalog services.

    Optional: include agent_id='my-agent-name' to tag this call for per-agent analytics
    in your dashboard at wayforth.io/dashboard/agents.

rail.title: Rail
rail.description: Payment rail. 'managed' uses Wayforth's keys (recommended, zero setup). 'byok' uses your stored key.

input.title: Input
input.description: The actual content to process. Example: {'text': 'Hello world'} for translation, {'city': 'Tokyo'} for weather, {'query': 'AI news'} for search, {'symbol': 'AAPL'} for stocks

intent.title: Intent
intent.description: Natural language description of what you need. Example: 'translate this text to Spanish', 'get weather in Tokyo', 'search the web for AI news', 'get stock price for AAPL'

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Optional: tag this call with your agent's name for per-agent analytics in your dashboard. Example: 'translation-agent', 'my-chatbot'. Max 64 chars, alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores.

category.title: Category
category.description: Optional: filter by service category. Options: translation, inference, data, image, audio, communication

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_execute
init_ref_tools.description:
Execute any API service instantly.
    15 managed services run with zero API keys —
    Wayforth holds the credentials.
    The fastest way to add any API capability
    to your agent.

    Optional: include agent_id='my-agent-name' to tag this call for per-agent analytics
    in your dashboard at wayforth.io/dashboard/agents.

params.title: Params
params.description: Service-specific parameters as a JSON object (e.g. {'text': 'Hello', 'target_lang': 'ES'} for DeepL)

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: Optional: tag this call with your agent's name for per-agent analytics. Example: 'translation-agent'. Max 64 chars, alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores.

key_source.title: Key Source
key_source.description: Key source: 'managed' (use Wayforth's key, default) or 'byok' (use your stored key)

service_slug.title: Service Slug
service_slug.description: Service to call: groq, deepl, openweather, newsapi, serper, resend, assemblyai, stability, tavily, jina, alphavantage, elevenlabs — or any custom slug for BYOK

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_search
init_ref_tools.description:
Search 300+ verified APIs ranked by
    WayforthRank — real agent payment signals,
    not ads. Use this when you don't know
    which service to execute.

query.title: Query
query.description: Natural language description of the API service you need (e.g. 'translate text to Spanish', 'generate images')

category.title: Category
category.description: Optional category filter: inference, data, translation, image, code, audio, embeddings

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_list
init_ref_tools.description: Browse the Wayforth service catalog.

category.title: Category
category.description: Filter by category: inference, data, translation, image, code, audio, embeddings

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_stats
init_ref_tools.description: Get current Wayforth catalog statistics.

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_status
init_ref_tools.description: Return API health and catalog statistics.

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_query
init_ref_tools.description:
Structured service discovery using WayforthQL v2.
    More precise than wayforth_search — supports price caps, protocol filters,
    x402-only, provider filtering, and explicit sort order.
    Use when you need deterministic filtering rather than pure semantic ranking.

query.title: Query
query.description: Natural language query describing the API you need (e.g. 'fast cheap translation', 'image generation under $0.01')

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Pagination offset — skip this many results

sort_by.title: Sort By
sort_by.description: Sort order: 'wri' (WayforthRank score, default), 'price' (cheapest first), 'tier' (highest tier first)

category.title: Category

protocol.title: Protocol

price_max.title: Price Max

x402_only.title: X402 Only
x402_only.description: When true, return only x402-native services

verified_only.title: Verified Only
verified_only.description: When true, return only tier-2+ verified services

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_compare
init_ref_tools.description:
Compare 2-5 API services side by side.
    Returns WRI scores, response times, costs, signal counts and a plain-English recommendation.
    Use this before committing to a service.

query.title: Query
query.description: Optional: describe your use case to get a relevance score per service. Example: 'fast inference for my chatbot'

slugs.title: Slugs
slugs.description: Comma-separated service slugs to compare. Example: 'groq,together,perplexity'. Compare 2-5 services at a time.

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_similar
init_ref_tools.description:
Find services similar to or commonly used alongside a given service.
    Returns co-usage patterns from real agent behavior.

service_id.title: Service Id
service_id.description: Service ID or wayforth:// identifier to find co-used services for

init_ref_tools.name: wayforth_pay
init_ref_tools.description:
Pay for a service through Wayforth.

    Two payment tracks:

    track='card' (default — no crypto needed):
      - Deducts from your Wayforth credit balance
      - Stripe Treasury processes the payment to the service
      - Get credits at wayforth.io/dashboard → Billing → Card Track

    track='crypto' (non-custodial — your wallet):
      - Returns Base calldata for you to broadcast
      - Your USDC, your wallet, fully on-chain
      - Non-custodial — Wayforth never holds your funds

    Routing fee: 1.5% on all tracks

zip.description: 5-digit US ZIP code. Used with lastName for name-mode (combines with city/state).

city.description: City name. Used with lastName for name-mode OR with address + state for address-mode.

state.description: Two-letter US state code (e.g. CA, NY, TX). Used with lastName for name-mode OR with address + city for address-mode.

address.description: Street address. Required for address-mode searches (must combine with city + state). Free-form line, no normalization needed.

lastName.description: Person's last name. Required for name-mode searches (must combine with city, state, or zip).

firstName.description: Person's first name. Optional but recommended for name-mode searches. Combines with lastName + locality (city/state/zip). Nickname expansion controlled by nicknameSearch.

middleName.description: Person's middle name. Optional. Tightens name-mode match precision; rarely required.

addressRecency.description: Filter address-based search results by how recently a person was linked to the search address. `all` = no recency filter (broadest, default when omitted); `current` = address is the subject's current residence; `lastOneYear` / `lastThreeYears` / `lastFiveYears` / `lastTenYears` = include only people linked within the past 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 years. Only applies to address-based searches.

nicknameSearch.description: Controls how aggressively firstName is expanded to spelling/nickname variants. `true` (default) = broad expansion (Megan → Meagan, Meggan, Meg; Jon → John, Jonathan; Katie → Katy, Kate). `false` = narrower expansion — drops loose nickname variants but the dataset may still surface tight phonetic neighbors (observed: searching firstName=MEGAN with nicknameSearch=false still returned MEAGAN at rank 0 when she was the strongest local match). Pass `false` to reduce noise from long-form variants; do NOT rely on `false` for strict literal-spelling-only matching.

init_ref_tools.description: Expand a stub id (a relative, associate, or property owner referenced in a prior `search_person_or_address` or `expand_person_record` result) into a full record. Billed 1 credit per non-null result. To re-read a record from an existing search, use `get_search_history` (free).

pid.description: Person identifier from a prior search's result entry. Returned on every record in search_person_or_address responses; pass it here to fetch the full record for that person. Costs 1 credit per non-null expansion (matching search_person_or_address pricing).

init_ref_tools.name: get_search_history

Four call modes: (1) no args → list recent searches and return current credit balance in the response envelope (use this when the user asks how many credits they have left); (2) `searchId` → re-read trimmed envelope; (3) `searchId + pid` → full record for one hit; (4) `searchId + offset + limit` → paged slice of full records (default limit 5, max 25). Use this for follow-ups on existing results — do NOT call `search_person_or_address` again to drill in. Zero credits consumed.

pid.description: Person identifier within a stored search. Pass with searchId to expand that one record from the stored result to its full form. Free.

limit.description: Max records to return (1-25). Default depends on mode: 20 for list-mode, 5 for paged-slice mode.

offset.description: Zero-based offset for pagination. Used with limit in paged-slice mode (searchId + offset/limit).

searchId.description: Identifier from a prior search response (meta.searchId). Pass alone to re-emit the trimmed envelope; pass with pid for full-record expansion; pass with offset/limit for paged full records. All four modes are free (no credit consumed).

environment.description: A research and data-retrieval service that searches the live web and a continuously updated index of authoritative structured data. It supports discovering available datasets, retrieving specific metrics or time series, generating cited answers, rendering visualizations, and fetching underlying rows or full source content for deeper analysis.

init_ref_tools.name: tako_answer
init_ref_tools.description:
Ask one specific data question; get one synthesized answer grounded in the data or web tako cites.

Best for: a single, self-contained data question with one answer. The `answer` is synthesized from the cited sources; the `cards` are its citations.

`tako_search` is the counterpart for fast, parallel retrieval of data cards; the Tako Answer Agent handles open-ended, multi-step research.

Grounds over BOTH data and web by default. When unsure the proprietary data exists or its exact name, run `tako_available_data` first (free, instant) — the recommended first step — then pin the node_ids it returns here for an accurate, grounded answer. To read the full rows or page text behind any cited card or web result, call `tako_contents` on its url.

query.description: Natural-language question to answer (e.g. "What was US GDP in 2024?"). Website-traffic data is keyed by domain — ask about "openai.com monthly visits", not "OpenAI website visits".

strict.description: Hard filter. When true, return ONLY cards matching at least one node in node_ids (which must then be non-empty — empty node_ids + strict is a 400). When false (default), pinned nodes are preferred/boosted but organic results still return.

sources.description: Source(s) to ground in. Default ["data","web"] (both) — keep BOTH enabled unless you have a confirmed reason to narrow. Narrow to ["data"] only once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists (web is the fallback when it does not). Narrow to ["web"] only for content a data graph cannot hold (news articles, page text, qualitative claims) — never because a metric merely feels web-native: website traffic, app usage, and similar digital metrics ARE in the proprietary data graph. ("tako" is a legacy synonym for "data".)

node_ids.description: Graph node ids (from tako_available_data) to PIN into the proprietary data source. Pinned nodes get a strong retrieval boost. Max 20. Applies only to the 'data' source.

country_code.description: ISO country code for localized results.

content.description: Raw export descriptor + inline data preview. Read the sibling `exportable` boolean as the call/skip signal instead of inferring from this field's presence. Missing or null here is equivalent to exportable:false. Present is necessary for a tako_contents export but not a guarantee (a rare card still 403s — fall back to the preview/chart).

exportable.description: Whether this card's underlying data can be fetched with tako_contents. false → NOT exportable: do NOT call tako_contents on this card, use its inline preview/chart. true → eligible, but not a guarantee — a rare card still 403s, so on error fall back rather than retry.

url.description: The web page URL. Always fetchable via tako_contents for the page's full text (web urls need no `exportable` flag, unlike cards) — a fallback you can read when no Tako data card fits the query.

init_ref_tools.name: tako_available_data
init_ref_tools.description:
Find what proprietary, continuously-updated structured data exists on something — summarized in one call. Free and fast.

The recommended first step for a data lookup: run this before tako_search / tako_answer whenever you're unsure the data exists or its exact name. It's free, it confirms coverage, and the exact names it returns make the follow-up priced call land precisely instead of guessing. (Skip it only for an obvious open-web query that no data graph would hold.)

Best for: any "what structured/proprietary data is there on X?" question, and for confirming a specific figure actually exists BEFORE you spend a priced tako_search / tako_answer — a cheap accuracy check that tells you whether the data exists and under exactly what name.

Works on an entity (a company, person, or place → the metrics tracked on it, e.g. Tesla) or a metric (→ the entities it is tracked across, e.g. Inflation Rate).

Tips:
One metric across many entities → one metric-first call; one entity across many metrics → one entity-first call. The coverage.names answer all of them at once — never loop one call per name.
Pass `label` when you can categorize the term (company → ORG, country → GPE, person → PERSON) — a strong disambiguation boost.
Each match's coverage.names lists the exact metric/entity names — reuse them verbatim in a follow-up tako_search (e.g. "Apple Inc. revenue") to hit the data precisely.

q.description: Entity or metric name to look up (min 2 chars).

label.description: NER label to prefer (boost, not a filter). Supply when you can categorize the term (company→ORG, place→GPE, person→PERSON, ...).

types.description: Narrow resolution to a "thing" ("entity") or a "measure" ("metric"). Omit to search both.

found.description: True when at least one match has live data coverage — not mere node resolution. A resolved node with no coverage (or whose coverage lookup failed) yields false.

init_ref_tools.name: tako_contents
init_ref_tools.description:
Fetch the real content behind one result URL from tako_search or tako_answer — the rows behind a Tako card, or a web page's full text.

Best for: getting the full data to compute over or quote after `tako_search` / `tako_answer` — a search result carries only a preview and a chart, not its rows.

Precondition (Tako cards): only call this when the card's result had `exportable: true`. If `exportable` is false (equivalently, `content` is missing or null) this call fails — use the card's preview/chart instead, don't call. `exportable: true` is necessary but not sufficient: a rare card still 403s, so fall back, don't retry.

Web URLs always work — so this is also the fallback path when tako_search / tako_answer surfaced relevant `web_results` but no fitting Tako data card: pass the web result's url here to read its full page text.

url.description: The result URL to fetch downloadable content for (a TakoCard.webpage_url or a WebResult.url). A Tako card URL yields a CSV of the card's data; any other URL yields the page's extracted text.

mode.description: Delivery only — does NOT change the row cap: "inline" (default) returns the content in the response body (a Tako card — 20-row default, raise max_rows up to 2,000; total_rows/truncated report truncation — or web text) so you can read it directly; "url" returns a short-lived presigned download_url to the same capped file.

max_rows.description: Tako cards only: max CSV rows to return, in either delivery mode. Omit for the free 20-row default (baseline charge only); raise up to 2,000 to export more, billed per 1,000 rows beyond the free 20. Ignored for web URLs (always full text).

content_format.description: Tako cards only — serialization of the returned data: "csv" (default, returned as text in `data`), "json_records" (array of row objects in `records`), or "json_compact" (compact columns+rows TakoDataset in `dataset`). Ignored for web URLs (always text in `data`).

ref.description: Source URL the dataset was derived from (e.g. the Tako card URL).

rows.description: Row data as positional cell arrays aligned to `columns` order. Cells are string/number/boolean/null; nulls are preserved, never coerced.

type.description: Logical column type: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'date', or 'datetime'. Temporal cells are ISO-8601 strings.

items.description: Typed header entry; `type` is the JSON-facing column type.

init_ref_tools.name: tako_search
init_ref_tools.description:
Fastest, direct retrieval of data or metrics from the live web and proprietary data sources, returned as structured cards and web links; the top card auto-renders inline as a chart. It replaces a generic web search for data lookups.

Best for: grabbing a known figure or metric — a value, time series, price, score, schedule, forecast, poll, or prediction-market number. It is cheap and fast, built to fan out: many narrow queries fired in parallel retrieve far better than one broad query, and you assemble the multi-part result yourself.

Coverage spans economics, finance, company KPIs, demographics, sports, markets, weather, elections, prediction markets, website/app traffic, real estate, energy, health, and more — metrics that sound web-only (e.g. SimilarWeb-style website traffic) are in the data graph.

Each query resolves one entity + one metric ("Apple revenue", "Nvidia vs AMD gross margin"); broad or compound queries ("today's sports + odds") retrieve poorly. When unsure the data exists or its exact name, run `tako_available_data` first (free) — the recommended first step for a data lookup; it hands you the exact names to query here.

Data and web come back together — treat them as one result, not an either/or. Returns: `cards` (up to `count`) with preview rows and chart URLs, plus `web_results`. When no data card fits the query, the `web_results` can be your fallback: call `tako_contents` on the most relevant one's url to read its full page text (web urls are always fetchable; a card's full csv needs `exportable: true`).

If you aren’t prioritizing grabbing specific data or showing charts/tables, and just want a synthesized, written answer to a more specific data question, use `tako_answer` instead.

count.description: Maximum number of results to return per source (1-20).

query.description: Natural-language search query (e.g. "US GDP growth", "Intel vs Nvidia revenue"). Website-traffic data is keyed by domain — query "openai.com monthly visits", not "OpenAI website visits".

effort.description: Search effort: "fast" (default) or "instant" (fastest, serves cached embeds as-is). Omit for fast.

strict.description: Hard filter. When true, return ONLY cards matching at least one node in node_ids (which must then be non-empty — empty node_ids + strict is a 400). When false (default), pinned nodes are preferred/boosted but organic results still return.

sources.description: Source(s) to search. Default ["data","web"] (both) — keep BOTH enabled unless you have a confirmed reason to narrow. Narrow to ["data"] only once `tako_available_data` has confirmed the proprietary data exists (web is the fallback when it does not). Narrow to ["web"] only for content a data graph cannot hold (news articles, page text, qualitative claims) — never because a metric merely feels web-native: website traffic, app usage, and similar digital metrics ARE in the proprietary data graph. ("tako" is a legacy synonym for "data".)

node_ids.description: Graph node ids (from tako_available_data, or a card's nodes) to PIN into the proprietary data source. Pinned nodes get a strong retrieval boost. Max 20. Applies only to the 'data' source.

country_code.description: ISO country code for localized results.

include_contents.description: Inline each Tako card's free 5-row data preview (default true). Set false for pointers-only (title/chart/nodes, no rows) — cheaper for large parallel fan-outs. Controls the DATA source only; web page text is never auto-inlined (billed per page — use tako_contents). Full export is a separate tako_contents call — possible only for cards marked `exportable: true`.

content.description: Raw export descriptor + inline data preview. Read the sibling `exportable` boolean as the call/skip signal instead of inferring from this field's presence. Missing or null here is equivalent to exportable:false. Present is necessary for a tako_contents export but not a guarantee (a rare card still 403s — fall back to the preview/chart).

exportable.description: Whether this card's underlying data can be fetched with tako_contents. false → NOT exportable: do NOT call tako_contents on this card, use its inline preview/chart. true → eligible, but not a guarantee — a rare card still 403s, so on error fall back rather than retry.

url.description: The web page URL. Always fetchable via tako_contents for the page's full text (web urls need no `exportable` flag, unlike cards) — a fallback you can read when no Tako data card fits the query.

environment.description: bugAgent is an AI-native quality engineering platform that centralizes bug tracking, test-case and test-run management, Playwright and mobile automation, exploratory testing, performance testing, security scanning, AI code review, compliance evidence, and integrations such as Jira, GitHub, BrowserStack, and cloud services. It supports collaborative QA workflows from issue discovery and prioritization through assignment, remediation guidance, verification, reporting, and release readiness.

init_ref_tools.name: create_bug_report
init_ref_tools.description: File a new bug report. Auto-classifies bug type if not provided. Returns the created report with classification.

url.description: URL where the bug was found

type.description: Bug type — one of 19 categories matching the dashboard. Auto-classified if omitted.

project.description: Project slug or name to file the bug into. Use list_projects to see available projects. Falls back to default project if omitted.

priority.description: Fix urgency, independent of severity. urgent = drop everything, high = this sprint, normal = standard queue, low = backlog. Omit to leave unset.

severity.description: Bug severity. Prefer formal QA codes: s1 (Blocker), s2 (Critical), s3 (Major), s4 (Minor). Legacy values (critical/high/medium/low) still accepted. Auto-defaults to s3 when omitted.

assigned_to.description: User ID to assign this bug to. Use list_team_members to get valid user IDs.

data.description: Base64-encoded file content

mimeType.description: MIME type. Any image/* (png, jpeg, gif, webp, heic, avif, svg), video/* (mp4, webm, quicktime), audio/* (mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, webm), application/pdf, text/plain, text/csv, text/markdown, application/json

attachments.description: File attachments — any image, video, audio, PDF, or text/JSON file. Base64-encoded. Max 400 MB per file.

format_description.description: Set to true to reformat the description into a structured bug template using AI. When false (default), the description is stored exactly as provided.

time_spent_seconds.description: Time spent in seconds. Used for tracking QA effort. The timer on the dashboard saves exact seconds.

init_ref_tools.name: list_bug_reports
init_ref_tools.description: List bug reports with optional filters by type, severity, status, resolution, root cause, reporter, or search query. Each result includes reporter_user_id so you can see who filed each report. To filter by reporter name (e.g. "show reports by Johnson Russell"), first call list_team_members to find that person's userId, then pass it as reporter_user_id.

type.description: Filter by bug type — one of the 19 dashboard categories.

offset.description: Offset for pagination

status.description: Filter by status. Values match the dashboard's status options exactly — `new` (entry), `awaiting-triage` (waiting on a human answer), `confirmed`, `in-progress`, `retesting`, `resolved`, `reopened`, `closed`.

severity.description: Filter by severity. Accepts formal QA (s1-s4) or legacy (critical/high/medium/low) — stored rows may use either convention.

resolution.description: Filter by resolution. Set on transition out of `new` per the agent-loop convention — see https://app.bugagent.com/docs#section-bug-reports.

root_cause.description: Filter by root cause. Open-ended kebab-case taxonomy; common values today include `regression`, `missing-requirement`, `documentation`, `incomplete-refactor`, `not-a-bug`, `requirements-mismatch`. Exact-match — pass `regression` to find regression-class bugs only.

reporter_user_id.description: Filter to reports filed by a specific user. Pass a user UUID — call list_team_members first to find the right userId for a given name. Scoped to your team; cross-team IDs are silently filtered out by RLS.

init_ref_tools.name: pick_next_bug
init_ref_tools.description: Return the next bug(s) the agent loop should work on, ordered by priority (S1 → S2 → S3, oldest first within each bucket). Automatically scoped to your workspace — shows tickets across all projects in your team. READ-ONLY — does not atomically claim tickets. Use a separate claim flow (today: update_bug_report with status=in-progress; eventually: claim_bug per TEST-177) when actually picking up work. Returns rows in the same shape as list_bug_reports for tool composability.

limit.description: Maximum number of rows to return (default 1, max 50). Use 1 to grab the next ticket; use 5-10 to peek at the queue and deliberate before claiming.

severity.description: Filter to a single severity tier. Omit to get the highest-priority candidates across all three. S4 is intentionally excluded from the queue — manual cleanup territory.

init_ref_tools.name: claim_bug
init_ref_tools.description: Atomically claim a bug for the calling user. Sets status="in-progress", assigned_to=caller, and claimed_at=NOW() — but ONLY if the ticket is currently in status="new". Returns {claimed: true, bug} if the claim succeeded; {claimed: false, reason} if another consumer already claimed it (race-loser path) or the ticket no longer exists. Race-free via Postgres row-level lock — safe to call from multiple agents/replicas concurrently. Pair with pick_next_bug for the read-then-claim pattern.

id.description: Bug report ID to claim — UUID or short ID (e.g. TEST-BA-123).

init_ref_tools.name: get_bug_report
init_ref_tools.description: Get full details of a specific bug report by ID. Accepts either the UUID or the workspace-scoped short ID (e.g. TEST-BA-123). Short IDs are resolved within the caller's team only.

id.description: Bug report ID — UUID or short ID (e.g. TEST-BA-123)

init_ref_tools.name: update_bug_report
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing bug report. Only provided fields will be changed. Use assigned_to with a user ID from list_team_members to assign the bug to someone. Accepts either the UUID or the short ID (e.g. TEST-BA-123). Set `resolution` and `root_cause` whenever transitioning out of `new` — required by the agent-loop convention so analytics + Kanban render correctly.

id.description: Bug report ID to update — UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN)

type.description: New bug type — one of 19 categories matching the dashboard.

status.description: New status. Values match the dashboard exactly: `new`, `awaiting-triage`, `confirmed`, `in-progress`, `retesting`, `resolved`, `reopened`, `closed`. Note hyphens (not underscores) in `awaiting-triage` and `in-progress` — using underscores will write a literal underscore string the kanban won't recognise.

priority.description: New fix urgency, independent of severity. urgent = drop everything, high = this sprint, normal = standard queue, low = backlog.

severity.description: New severity. Prefer formal QA codes: s1 (Blocker), s2 (Critical), s3 (Major), s4 (Minor). Legacy values still accepted.

resolution.description: Resolution outcome — set whenever the row transitions out of `new` toward `retesting`/`resolved`/`closed`. `fixed` (code change shipped), `duplicate` (reference the canonical ticket in a comment), `works-as-designed` (intentional behavior), `cannot-reproduce`, `will-not-fix` (deliberately deferring), `need-more-info`.

root_cause.description: Root-cause category. Open-ended short hyphenated tags — common values: `regression`, `missing-requirement`, `documentation`, `incomplete-refactor`, `not-a-bug`, `requirements-mismatch`. Set alongside `resolution` on close. Free-form so the taxonomy can grow when a new pattern shows up in 2+ tickets.

assigned_to.description: User ID to assign this bug to. Use list_team_members to get valid user IDs. Set to empty string to unassign.

time_spent_seconds.description: Time spent in seconds. Used for tracking QA effort. The timer on the dashboard saves exact seconds.

init_ref_tools.name: push_to_claude
init_ref_tools.description: Generate (or regenerate) the Developer Notes for a bug report — root cause, affected areas, suggested fix, verification steps, and risk assessment. Internally runs a multi-step chain that adapts to severity: medium/low bugs get a three-step chain (Sonnet draft → OpenAI challenger critique → Sonnet synthesis); critical/high bugs escalate to a five-step debate (draft → critique → Sonnet rebuttal → adjudicator, where a different model — default Claude Opus — reads the full transcript and writes the final notes with independent judgment). The response exposes every round (draft, critique, rebuttal, challenger_model, adjudicator_model, debated flag) so agents can inspect the reasoning chain. Any step failing falls through to the next-best answer. Uses platform keys — no per-team Claude connection required. Auto-fires on bug creation. Accepts UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

report_id.description: Bug report ID to analyze — UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN)

init_ref_tools.name: analyze_fix_area
init_ref_tools.description: Generate (or regenerate) the "Likely Fix Area" for a bug report — a narrow Sonnet output that names where in the codebase the fix most likely belongs. Uses the platform Anthropic key (no per-team Claude connection required). When the project has a GitHub repo mapped and the team has a github_connections row, the output is grounded in real file snippets; otherwise it falls back to general guidance with a nudge to connect a repo. Writes the result back onto bug_reports (likely_fix_area, likely_fix_area_status, likely_fix_area_generated_at) so the dashboard picks it up automatically. Accepts UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

report_id.description: Bug report ID — UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN)

init_ref_tools.name: get_performance_results
init_ref_tools.description: Get results for a performance test run. Includes Lighthouse scores (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO), Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS, FCP, TTFB, INP, TBT, SI), and load test metrics (VUs, requests, RPS, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies).

init_ref_tools.name: get_performance_usage
init_ref_tools.description: Check monthly performance test usage against plan limits. Performance testing is Enterprise-only. Limits: Free=0, Team=0, Enterprise=unlimited, Admin=unlimited.

init_ref_tools.name: create_security_scan
init_ref_tools.description: Create a security scan configuration. Web: Quick Scanner + Nuclei + ZAP DAST. Mobile: MobSF binary analysis for APK/IPA. Code: Semgrep SAST for 30+ languages. Configurable auto-bug creation with severity threshold. Enterprise only.

url.description: Target URL for web scans (domain must be verified via DNS TXT record)

name.description: Name for the security scan config

app_id.description: Mobile app ID for mobile scans (from upload_mobile_app)

repo_url.description: Repository HTTPS clone URL for code scans

scan_type.description: Type of scan: web (DAST), mobile (binary analysis), or code (SAST)

repo_token.description: GitHub PAT with repo scope for private repos

scan_depth.description: Scan depth: quick (~30s), regular (~5min), deep (up to 30min). Default: quick

auto_create_bug.description: Auto-create bug reports for qualifying findings (default: true)

min_severity_for_bug.description: Minimum severity for auto-bug creation (default: high)

init_ref_tools.name: list_security_scans
init_ref_tools.description: List security scan configurations for the current team. Returns scan names, types, targets, and status.

init_ref_tools.name: run_security_scan
init_ref_tools.description: Trigger a security scan run. Web: Quick Scanner + Nuclei + ZAP. Mobile: MobSF binary analysis. Code: Semgrep SAST. Returns a run ID to poll for results.

scan_id.description: The security scan config ID to run

scan_depth.description: Override scan depth for this run

init_ref_tools.name: get_security_results
init_ref_tools.description: Get results for a security scan run. Includes findings categorized by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low, Info) with vulnerability type, description, affected URL/file, and remediation guidance.

init_ref_tools.name: get_security_usage
init_ref_tools.description: Check monthly security scan usage against plan limits. Security scanning is Enterprise-only. Limits: Enterprise=unlimited, Admin=unlimited.

init_ref_tools.name: list_code_reviews

init_ref_tools.name: get_code_review
init_ref_tools.description: Get a code review with all findings. Each finding includes severity, category (bug/security/performance/style/logic/maintainability), title, description, code suggestion, file path, and line numbers.

init_ref_tools.name: get_code_review_usage
init_ref_tools.description: Check monthly code review usage. AI code review is Enterprise-only. Enterprise: unlimited. Free and Team: 0.

init_ref_tools.name: get_code_review_analytics
init_ref_tools.description: Get code review analytics: trends, finding categories/sources, severity breakdown, velocity metrics, top repos, top authors. Enterprise only.

days.description: Lookback period in days (7, 30, or 90). Default: 30.

init_ref_tools.name: list_explorations
init_ref_tools.description: List Exploratory AI configs for the team. Each exploration targets a URL and can be run to autonomously find bugs.

init_ref_tools.name: create_exploration
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new Exploratory AI config. The exploration will autonomously crawl the target URL, generate test scripts, execute them, and file bug reports for issues found. Enterprise only.

instructions.description: Detailed testing instructions and business logic context

init_ref_tools.name: get_exploration
init_ref_tools.description: Get an exploration config with its recent runs.

init_ref_tools.name: get_exploration_run
init_ref_tools.description: Get results of an exploration run including all findings, phase data, and linked bugs.

init_ref_tools.name: get_exploration_usage
init_ref_tools.description: Check monthly Exploratory AI usage. Exploratory AI is Enterprise-only. Enterprise: unlimited.

init_ref_tools.name: flush_reports
init_ref_tools.description: Bulk delete old bug reports. Only team owners and admins can flush. Optionally limit to a specific project.

months.description: Delete reports older than this many months (1-12)

project.description: Limit to a specific project slug

init_ref_tools.name: generate_api_key
init_ref_tools.description: Create a named API key. The full key is returned only once — save it securely.

name.description: Human-readable name for the key (e.g. "CI Pipeline", "Staging Server")

init_ref_tools.name: list_api_keys
init_ref_tools.description: List your active API keys. Shows key prefix (first 16 chars) but never the full key.

init_ref_tools.name: regenerate_api_key
init_ref_tools.description: Revoke an existing API key and create a new one with the same name and scopes. The new key is returned only once.

key_id.description: ID of the API key to regenerate

init_ref_tools.name: delete_api_key
init_ref_tools.description: Revoke and delete an API key. The key will immediately stop working.

key_id.description: ID of the API key to delete

init_ref_tools.name: check_jira_sync
init_ref_tools.description: Check if a Jira-synced bug report has remote changes. Returns field differences and new Jira comments. Use before merge_jira_sync.

id.description: Bug report ID (must be synced to Jira)

init_ref_tools.name: merge_jira_sync
init_ref_tools.description: Bi-directional merge between bugAgent and Jira. Updates both systems to match. Use check_jira_sync first to see differences.

prefer.description: Which side to prefer for all conflicting fields (default: bugagent)

init_ref_tools.name: add_comment
init_ref_tools.description: Add a comment to a bug report. If the report is synced to Jira, the comment is automatically pushed to the Jira issue. Accepts UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN). Pass author_user_id to post the comment as a specific agent account (the target user must have is_agent=true — use list_team_members to find the Claude bot user ID).

content.description: Comment text

report_id.description: Bug report ID — UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN)

author_user_id.description: Post the comment as this user instead of the authenticated caller. Only accepted when the target profile has is_agent=true — prevents impersonating real users. Use list_team_members to find the Claude bot user ID (claude-bot@bugagent.com).

init_ref_tools.name: list_comments
init_ref_tools.description: List all comments on a bug report, oldest first, with author names. Comments are not part of get_bug_report — use this to read the discussion thread on a ticket. Accepts UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

report_id.description: Bug report ID — UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN)

init_ref_tools.name: link_bug_reports
init_ref_tools.description: Create a directional link between two bug reports. Use `duplicate-of` to mark one report as a duplicate of another, `parent-of` for parent/child hierarchies, `related-to` for a non-directional related-issue link, and `depends-on` to record that the from-report cannot ship until the to-report does. Both reports must be in the same workspace. Accepts UUIDs or short IDs (PREFIX-NNN).

link_type.description: The relationship type. `duplicate-of`/`parent-of`/`depends-on` are directional (the inverse view — duplicated-by, subtask-of, blocks — is derived at read time). `related-to` is symmetric.

to_report_id.description: The "to" side of the link — the report being referenced. UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

from_report_id.description: The "from" side of the link — the report whose perspective the link_type describes. UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

init_ref_tools.name: unlink_bug_reports
init_ref_tools.description: Remove a previously-created bug-report link by its UUID. Use list_bug_report_links to find the link_id.

link_id.description: The UUID of the link to remove (returned by link_bug_reports or list_bug_report_links).

init_ref_tools.name: list_bug_report_links
init_ref_tools.description: List every user-curated link touching a bug report. Returns the link as it reads from this report's perspective — a stored `duplicate-of` row where this report is the target renders as `duplicated-by`, a `parent-of` row where this report is the target renders as `subtask-of`, and `depends-on` rows where this report is the target render as `blocks`. `related-to` is symmetric. Accepts UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

report_id.description: Bug report ID — UUID or short ID (PREFIX-NNN).

init_ref_tools.name: list_team_members
init_ref_tools.description: List all members of your current team/workspace with their roles and status.

init_ref_tools.name: invite_team_member

init_ref_tools.name: create_automation
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new automation with a custom Playwright script (no FAB recording required). Returns the automation ID. Team plan required. To duplicate an existing automation, first call get_automation to retrieve the script, then call this tool with name set to "[Copy] Original Name" and pass the original script, target_url, and project_id. The duplicate starts in draft status with no version history.

script.description: Playwright test script content. Defaults to a placeholder template if not provided.

project_id.description: Project to assign to. Uses default project if omitted.

init_ref_tools.name: list_automations
init_ref_tools.description: List Playwright automation scripts for the current team. Filter by project or status.

init_ref_tools.name: get_automation
init_ref_tools.description: Get full details of a Playwright automation script including the generated script code, recent run history, and the saved script_versions stack. Inspect script_versions (array of { script, source, timestamp }, oldest-first, capped at 100) before calling run_automation with version_index if you need to replay a specific historical version; omit version_index to run the current live script.

init_ref_tools.name: run_automation
init_ref_tools.description: Trigger an immediate run of a Playwright automation script. Runs on virtual headless browser by default, or on a real BrowserStack browser when browserstack=true. Pass version_index to replay a historical version of the script instead of the current live one.

bs_os.description: BrowserStack OS: Windows or OS X

device.description: Virtual mode device to emulate. Default: desktop

bs_browser.description: BrowserStack browser: chrome, firefox, safari, edge

browserstack.description: Set to true to run on a real BrowserStack browser instead of virtual

automation_id.description: The automation ID to run. Use list_automations to find IDs.

version_index.description: Replay a prior entry from the automation's script_versions stack (0 = oldest). DEFAULT: the current live script runs whenever this field is omitted or null — do not pass a placeholder value just to "pick current". Non-integer, negative, or out-of-range values are rejected rather than silently falling back. Call get_automation first to inspect available versions.

init_ref_tools.name: list_automation_runs
init_ref_tools.description: List recent runs for a Playwright automation script with status, duration, and error details.

automation_id.description: The automation ID to list runs for

init_ref_tools.name: list_schedules
init_ref_tools.description: List all scheduled automation runs for the current team with cron expression, timezone, and notification settings.

init_ref_tools.name: create_schedule
init_ref_tools.description: Create a scheduled automation run. Specify cron expression, timezone, and optional failure notifications (email, slack, or both).

device.description: Device to emulate. Options: desktop, macbook-air, iphone-15, galaxy-s23, ipad, etc. Default: desktop

init_ref_tools.name: delete_schedule
init_ref_tools.description: Delete a scheduled automation run.

init_ref_tools.name: list_mobile_schedules
init_ref_tools.description: List all scheduled mobile automation runs for the current team.

init_ref_tools.name: create_mobile_schedule
init_ref_tools.description: Create a scheduled mobile automation run on a real device.

automation_id.description: The mobile automation ID to schedule

init_ref_tools.name: delete_mobile_schedule
init_ref_tools.description: Delete a scheduled mobile automation run.

id.description: The mobile schedule ID to delete

init_ref_tools.name: list_security_schedules
init_ref_tools.description: List all scheduled security scans for the current team. Includes web DAST, code SAST, and mobile binary analysis scans.

init_ref_tools.name: create_security_schedule
init_ref_tools.description: Create a scheduled security scan. One schedule per scan config. Every run counts against your monthly security scan cap (Team 50/mo, Enterprise unlimited). Admin users bypass the cap. Scan depth is read from the scan config at run time — edit the config to change it.

scan_id.description: The security scan config ID to schedule. Use list_security_scans to find IDs.

notify_on_fail.description: Notify when the scan creates bug reports (default: none)

init_ref_tools.name: delete_security_schedule
init_ref_tools.description: Delete a scheduled security scan.

id.description: The security schedule ID to delete

init_ref_tools.name: optimize_automation_script
init_ref_tools.description: Send a Playwright automation script to Sonnet 4 for AI-powered optimization. Applies a 12-point checklist that automatically fixes selectors, wait strategies, assertions, error handling, auth patterns, mobile compatibility, and strict mode issues. The current script version is saved before optimization so you can undo the change.

automation_id.description: The automation ID to optimize. Use list_automations to find IDs.

init_ref_tools.name: undo_automation_script
init_ref_tools.description: Revert an automation script to its previous version. Up to 10 previous versions are retained. Versions are saved before manual edits, AI optimization, and script regeneration.

automation_id.description: The automation ID to undo. Use list_automations to find IDs.

init_ref_tools.name: list_notes
init_ref_tools.description: List testing notes. Shows both private notes and shared team notes. Filter by project, folder, or search keyword. Pass folder_id="unfiled" to list notes with no folder.

folder_id.description: Filter by folder ID, or pass "unfiled" to list notes not in any folder

init_ref_tools.name: get_note
init_ref_tools.description: Get full content of a specific note by ID.

init_ref_tools.name: create_note
init_ref_tools.description: Create a testing note. Supports markdown, plain text, bug template, checklist, and outline formats. Notes can be private or shared with the team. Optionally file into a folder (use list_note_folders to find folder IDs). Optionally attach base64-encoded files (images, video, audio, PDF, text/JSON) up to 400 MB each — same policy as bug report attachments.

title.description: Note title (auto-generated from content if empty)

format.description: Writing format (default: markdown)

content.description: Note content

folder_id.description: Folder to file the note under. Use list_note_folders to get IDs. Omit to leave unfiled.

project_id.description: Project to associate the note with

visibility.description: private = only you, shared = visible to team (default: private)

data.description: Base64-encoded file content

mimeType.description: MIME type. Any image/*, video/*, audio/*, application/pdf, text/plain, text/csv, text/markdown, or application/json

attachments.description: File attachments — any image, video, audio, PDF, or text/JSON file. Base64-encoded. Max 400 MB per file.

time_spent_seconds.description: Time spent in seconds. Used for tracking QA effort. The timer on the dashboard saves exact seconds.

init_ref_tools.name: update_note
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing note. Only the author can update their notes. Attachments passed in this call are APPENDED to the existing attachment list (existing attachments are preserved). Pass folder_id to move the note into a folder, or null to unfile it.

format.description: New format

content.description: New content

folder_id.description: Folder to move the note into, or null to unfile it

data.description: Base64-encoded file content

mimeType.description: MIME type. Any image/*, video/*, audio/*, application/pdf, text/plain, text/csv, text/markdown, or application/json

attachments.description: Additional attachments to append to the note. Max 400 MB per file.

time_spent_seconds.description: Time spent in seconds. Used for tracking QA effort. The timer on the dashboard saves exact seconds.

init_ref_tools.name: delete_note
init_ref_tools.description: Delete a note. Only the author can delete their notes.

init_ref_tools.name: list_note_folders
init_ref_tools.description: List all note folders for the team. Returns folder names, IDs, and note counts. Use folder IDs with create_note or update_note to file notes.

init_ref_tools.name: create_note_folder
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new note folder. Folders let teams organise notes into sections (e.g. "Onboarding", "Release Notes", "Test Strategy"). Use the returned folder ID with create_note or update_note to file notes into the folder.

sort_order.description: Sort position in the sidebar (lower = higher). Defaults to 0.

init_ref_tools.name: scale_team
init_ref_tools.description: Instantly scale your QA team with booster testers. Accounts are provisioned automatically with tester access. Available on the Team plan.

duration.description: Duration of the engagement (e.g. "1 week", "1 month", "3 months")

team_size.description: Number of tester accounts to provision (1-10)

product_url.description: URL of the product to be tested

init_ref_tools.name: list_time_entries
init_ref_tools.description: List time tracking entries for the team. Filter by period, project, or category. Team plan only.

period.description: Time period to filter by (default: all)

category.description: Filter by category

init_ref_tools.name: create_time_entry
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new time tracking entry. Log hours spent on QA tasks with categories. Team plan only.

category.description: Category (e.g. "testing", "bug-triage", "automation", "review", "meeting")

entry_date.description: Date for the entry in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)

init_ref_tools.name: update_time_entry
init_ref_tools.description: Update an existing time tracking entry. Team plan only.

category.description: Updated category

init_ref_tools.name: delete_time_entry
init_ref_tools.description: Delete a time tracking entry. Team plan only.

init_ref_tools.name: list_test_cases
init_ref_tools.description: List test cases with optional search, priority, type, status, and sort filters.

search.description: Keyword search across test case names

init_ref_tools.name: create_test_case
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new test case. Two template variants: "steps" (default) — per-step Action + Expected Result grid (pass `steps`); "text" — single free-form description of the steps (pass `text_content`). Both columns can be sent in the same call; the platform stores both independently so a tester switching templates later doesn't lose either side's data.

tags.description: Tags for categorization

urls.description: Reference URLs attached to the case. Max 10 entries. http/https only — other protocols are rejected server-side. (File attachments use a separate dashboard endpoint and are not exposed via MCP.)

action.description: Action to perform

steps.description: Test steps — used when template_type is "steps". Even when sending template_type="text" it is OK to also pass `steps`; the row stores both, so a future template flip restores them.

text_content.description: Free-form text describing the steps — used when template_type is "text". Multiple lines OK; newlines render as line breaks during a test run. Even when sending template_type="steps" it is OK to also pass `text_content`; the row stores both.

template_type.description: Template variant. "steps" (default) uses the per-step Action/Expected grid via the `steps` array. "text" uses the free-form description via `text_content`.

init_ref_tools.name: get_test_case
init_ref_tools.description: Get full test case details including steps and execution history.

init_ref_tools.name: list_test_suites
init_ref_tools.description: List test suites with case count and last run status.

init_ref_tools.name: create_test_suite
init_ref_tools.description: Create a test suite (folder). Pass parent_suite_id to nest under another suite. Max nesting depth is 3 levels (root/child/grandchild/great-grandchild).

parent_suite_id.description: UUID of parent suite to nest under. Omit for a root-level suite.

init_ref_tools.name: bulk_update_test_cases
init_ref_tools.description: Apply a single action to many test cases at once. Supported actions: set_priority, set_status, set_type, add_tags, remove_tags, add_to_suite, pin, unpin. Up to 500 case IDs per call. IDs not in your team are silently skipped.

action.description: Action to apply

params.description: Action params: { priority }, { status }, { type }, { tags: [...] }, { suite_id }

init_ref_tools.name: link_test_case_to_bug
init_ref_tools.description: Link a test case to a bug report — establishes traceability so the case shows up on the bug report and vice versa. The test case is recorded as proving (or covering or relating to) the linked bug.

init_ref_tools.name: list_test_case_links
init_ref_tools.description: List all requirement / bug links for a single test case.

init_ref_tools.name: list_test_case_review_candidates
init_ref_tools.description: List test cases the system has flagged as candidates for archival: never_run (no runs in 90+ days since creation), always_passes (5+ runs in last 90 days, all passed — possibly redundant), always_skipped (3+ runs in last 90 days, all skipped). Informational only — no auto-archive.

init_ref_tools.name: mark_test_case_review_flags
init_ref_tools.description: Persists current archive-candidate flags onto test_cases.review_flag for the team. Idempotent: clears stale flags before applying current ones. Safe to call any time; runs automatically every Monday at 09:00 UTC via pg_cron, but you can invoke on demand.

init_ref_tools.name: list_test_runs
init_ref_tools.description: List test runs with suite name, assignee, and pass/fail summary.

init_ref_tools.name: create_test_run
init_ref_tools.description: Create a test run from a suite. Snapshots all cases at creation time — INCLUDING every case in every descendant sub-suite (running a parent suite executes its whole subtree). A case linked to both a parent and a sub-suite is added exactly once.

suite_id.description: Test suite ID — every descendant sub-suite's cases are included too

init_ref_tools.name: list_test_case_folders
init_ref_tools.description: List folders for the authenticated team. Folders organize test cases hierarchically (one folder per case via test_cases.folder_id) — distinct from suites, which are many-to-many test-plan groupings. Returns up to 500 folders ordered by sort_order then name.

parent_folder_id.description: Return only direct children of this folder; use "root" for top-level folders

init_ref_tools.name: create_test_case_folder
init_ref_tools.description: Create a new test case folder. Nestable up to 3 levels deep via parent_folder_id. Folders organize the case catalog — use bulk_update_test_cases with action "set_folder" (via params.folder_id) to move cases into one.

parent_folder_id.description: Parent folder UUID; omit for a root-level folder

init_ref_tools.name: get_test_reports_overview
init_ref_tools.description: Headline quality KPIs for a time window — pass rate, runs completed, cases executed — with deltas vs the prior equivalent window. Same numbers the Reports tab KPI strip shows. Default window is the trailing 30 days.

suite_id.description: Optional suite filter; expands to the suite + all descendants

init_ref_tools.name: get_test_reports_failures
init_ref_tools.description: Failure analysis for the window — four parallel "what to fix?" lists: failing_cases (>=50% fail, min 3 runs), flaky_cases (most pass/fail flips), failing_suites (>=30% fail, min 5 runs), regressed_cases (most-recent fail with an earlier pass in the window). Same data the Reports tab failure-analysis grid shows.

suite_id.description: Optional suite filter; expands to the suite + all descendants

init_ref_tools.name: create_geo_snap
init_ref_tools.description: Capture screenshots of a URL from multiple countries simultaneously using real geo-IP routing. Verify localization, geo-redirects, and compliance.

url.description: The URL to capture screenshots of

countries.description: Array of country codes (e.g. ["US", "DE", "JP"]). Geo-Snap is Team/Enterprise; capture as many countries as you like, bounded by your workspace storage cap.

init_ref_tools.name: upload_mobile_app
init_ref_tools.description: Upload an APK (Android) or IPA (iOS) mobile app for testing on real devices.

file_url.description: Publicly accessible URL to the APK or IPA binary

init_ref_tools.name: update_mobile_app
init_ref_tools.description: Replace a mobile app binary with a new version. Deletes old file, clears cached URLs, and all automations use the new version on next run.

app_id.description: UUID of the mobile app to update

file_url.description: Publicly accessible URL to the new APK or IPA binary

init_ref_tools.name: create_mobile_automation
init_ref_tools.description: Create an Appium or Maestro YAML test script for a mobile app. Returns the automation ID. Enterprise only. To duplicate an existing automation, first call get_automation to retrieve the script, then call this tool with name set to "[Copy] Original Name" and pass the original script, target_url, and project_id. The duplicate starts in draft status with no version history.

app_id.description: UUID of the uploaded mobile app

script.description: The test script content (Appium Python, Appium JS, or Maestro YAML)

script_type.description: Script type: appium (Python), maestro (YAML), or appium_js (JavaScript)

init_ref_tools.name: run_mobile_test
init_ref_tools.description: Trigger a mobile test run on a real device. All script types (YAML, Appium Python, Appium JS) run on BrowserStack real devices via Appium 2.x W3C protocol. Video, Appium logs, device logs, and network logs are collected automatically.

automation_id.description: UUID of the mobile automation to run

init_ref_tools.name: list_mobile_runs
init_ref_tools.description: List mobile test run results with video recordings, screenshots, device logs, and performance metrics. Archived runs excluded by default.

init_ref_tools.name: collect_compliance_evidence
init_ref_tools.description: Trigger compliance evidence collection from connected services (Cloudflare, GitHub, Sentry, Supabase, Railway). Returns run ID for tracking. Enterprise only.

init_ref_tools.name: check_config_drift
init_ref_tools.description: Check all connected services for security configuration drift from baselines (SSL, HSTS, WAF, headers). Enterprise only.

init_ref_tools.name: generate_access_review
init_ref_tools.description: Generate a quarterly access review report showing team members, API key usage, MFA status, and recommendations. Enterprise only.

quarter.description: Quarter to review (e.g., "2026-Q2"). Defaults to current quarter.

init_ref_tools.name: get_security_events
init_ref_tools.description: Query the cross-service security event timeline (Cloudflare WAF, Sentry errors, etc.). Filter by source and severity. Enterprise only.

source.description: Filter by source: cloudflare, sentry, github, supabase, bugagent

severity.description: Filter by severity: critical, high, medium, low, info

apiKey.title: bugAgent API Key
apiKey.description: From app.bugagent.com → Settings → API Keys. Starts with ba_live_

environment.description: FavCRM is a hosted, agent-oriented CRM and operations platform for service businesses. It provides typed workflows for customer and contact management, segmentation, loyalty programs, bookings and capacity-aware scheduling, staff and resource availability, invoices and subscriptions, products and orders, support tickets, sales deals, marketing campaigns, messaging, CMS publishing, and internal approval workflows. Customer-facing messages and campaign sends require merchant approval through Workroom, while many records can be safely prepared as drafts. Access is via an API key and the hosted MCP endpoint at api.favcrm.io/mcp.

init_ref_tools.name: manage_profiles
init_ref_tools.description:
Create, update, or delete profiles. Two profile types:

HOUSEHOLD PROFILE (one per account, auto-created):
- Stores meal planning rules, schedules, cooking preferences
- 2000 char notes limit for storing: meal rules, day templates, schedules, prep preferences
- Cannot be deleted (edit only)
- Does NOT count against profile limit
- Triggers: 'save meal preferences', 'update household settings', 'set meal rules'
- FREE ACCOUNTS: Use Household profile for ALL dietary needs (individual profiles not available)

PERSON PROFILES (available on paid accounts only):
- Stores individual dietary needs, likes/dislikes, health goals
- 1000 char notes limit for individual preferences
- Counts against profile limit (up to 15)
- Triggers: 'add profile for X', 'X is vegetarian', 'add allergy for Y'

⚠️ BEFORE CREATING PERSON PROFILES:
- FIRST call show_profiles to check account tier
- If show_profiles returns "ACCOUNT TYPE: FREE" - do NOT attempt to create person profiles
- Simply say "Individual profiles aren't available on this account" without calling this tool

⚠️ FREE ACCOUNT BEHAVIOR (CRITICAL - FOLLOW EXACTLY):
- Individual profiles are NOT available on free accounts
- When you get error "INDIVIDUAL_PROFILES_NOT_AVAILABLE":
  1. STOP immediately - do not make any more tool calls
  2. Do NOT offer alternatives or workarounds
  3. Do NOT update Household notes with the person's info
  4. Do NOT suggest adding names to notes
  5. Simply say: "Individual profiles aren't available on this account."
  6. Then move on - do not dwell on it or offer solutions

DELETE: 'remove X profile' (person profiles only, cannot delete household)

REPLACE vs MERGE NOTES:
- Default (replaceNotes=false): New notes merge with existing likes/dislikes
- replaceNotes=true: Completely overwrite notes (use for fixing corrupted data)

HOUSEHOLD NOTES FORMAT:
MEAL RULES: one pasta night/week, no casseroles
DAY TEMPLATES: Monday = quick 15-20 min
SCHEDULE: Lila gymnastics Mon 5-7
PREP PREFERENCES: chicken shredded only

name.description: Profile name (required for create). Use "Household" for the household settings profile.

init_ref_tools.description: Ping the MCP server to check if it is running

init_ref_tools.name: list_bases
init_ref_tools.description:
Lists all bases that you have access to in your Airtable account.
Use this to get the baseId of the base you want to use.
Favorited and recently viewed bases are generally more relevant.
If the response includes an offset, pass it in a subsequent call to retrieve the next page of results.

offset.description: Pagination cursor from a previous list_bases response. Pass this to retrieve the next page of results.

isFavorite.description: Whether the base is a favorite.

permissionLevel.description: The permission level of the base. If "none", the user has interface-only access — use list_pages_for_base instead of list_tables_for_base to fetch data sources.

recentlyViewedTimestamp.description: The timestamp of the last time the base was viewed by the user.

offset.description: Pagination cursor. If present, pass this value as the offset parameter in a subsequent list_bases call to retrieve the next page of results.

init_ref_tools.name: list_workspaces
init_ref_tools.description:
Lists all workspaces the current user has access to, along with their permission level in each.
No dependencies. This is typically the first tool to call when you need a workspaceId.

offset.description: Pagination offset from the previous response. Pass this to retrieve the next page of results. Omit for the first page.
Pass the offset from a previous response to fetch the next page.

permissionLevel.description: The permission level of the current user in this workspace. "read" allows reading workspace data, "comment" allows commenting on records in bases within the workspace, "edit" allows modifying existing data, "create" allows creating new bases, "owner" allows full control of the workspace. Ordered from least to most privileged: "read", "comment", "edit", "create", "owner".

init_ref_tools.name: search_bases
init_ref_tools.description:
Searches for bases by name.
This is useful when you need to find a specific base quickly by a partial name-based match.
Returns bases sorted by their relevance score, as well as a recommended base ID and a hint on whether
we need to ask the user to explicitly select the base they want to use.

searchQuery.description:
The query to search for bases by name.
The search is case-insensitive and works with partial matches.
Examples: "projects", "issues", "customers"

hint.description: A hint on whether we need to ask the user to explicitly select the base they want to use.

score.description: The relevance score of the base.

isFavorite.description: Whether the base is a favorite.

permissionLevel.description: The permission level of the base. If "none", the user has interface-only access — use list_pages_for_base instead of list_tables_for_base to fetch data sources.

recentlyViewedTimestamp.description: The timestamp of the last time the base was viewed by the user.

recommendedBaseId.description: The ID of the recommended base. Undefined if no recommended base is found.

init_ref_tools.name: list_tables_for_base
init_ref_tools.description:
Gets the summary of a specific base. This includes the schemas of all tables in the
base, including field name and type.
If the base is not found or returns a permission error, the user may have interface-only access. Try list_pages_for_base instead.

baseId.description:
The ID of the base to get the summary of.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

primaryFieldId.description: The ID of the primary field.

init_ref_tools.name: get_table_schema
init_ref_tools.description:
Gets the detailed schema information for specified tables and fields in a base.
This returns the field ID, type, and config for the specified fields of the specified tables.
Example: get schema for two fields in a table:
{"baseId": "appZfrNIUEip5MazD", "tables": [{"tableId": "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG", "fieldIds": ["fld8WsrpLHHevsnW8", "fldgD18XtsueoiguT"]}]}

baseId.description:
The ID of the base containing the tables.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

fieldIds.description: The IDs of the fields to get schema information for.

tables.description:
An array of table IDs and corresponding field IDs to get schema information for.
Must start with "tbl" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "tblGlReoTNWfYnXIG".
Do not substitute user-facing names for tableId.
To get tableId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.
Field IDs must start with "fld" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV".
Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
To get fieldId, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

config.description: Type-specific configuration options for the field.

init_ref_tools.name: list_records_for_table
init_ref_tools.description:
Lists records queried from an Airtable table.
Do not assume baseId and tableId. Obtain these from search_bases → list_tables_for_base.
Do not attempt to pass filterByFormula. Look carefully at the filters parameter.
Pre-requisite: If filtering on singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, and the choice name is not provided, you must call get_table_schema first to get the choice IDs.
Aim to provide at least 6 relevant fields via the 'fieldIds' parameter.
Note: singleSelect and multipleSelects field values are returned as objects (e.g., {"id": "sel...", "name": "Option", "color": "blue"}) or arrays of such objects. When writing these values back via create_records_for_table or update_records_for_table, use the plain string name (e.g., "Option") instead of the object.
If the base is not found or returns a permission error, the user may have interface-only access. Try list_records_for_page instead.

fieldId.description: The field to sort by. Accepts either a field ID (e.g., "fldGlRtkBNWfYnPOV") or field name (e.g., "Status").

sort.description:
A list of sort objects that specifies how the records will be ordered.
Each sort object must have a fieldId key specifying the field to sort on (ID or name), and an optional direction key that is either "asc" or "desc".
The default direction is "asc".
Records are sorted by the first sort object first, then by the second sort object for records that have the same value for the first sort, and so on.
Example sort by a single field in descending order: [{"fieldId": "Status", "direction": "desc"}]
Example sort by two fields, first ascending then descending: [{"fieldId": "Priority", "direction": "asc"}, {"fieldId": "Created", "direction": "desc"}]

baseId.description:
The ID of the base containing the table.
Must start with "app" and is 17 characters long.
Example: "appZfrNIUEip5MazD".
Do not substitute user-facing names for baseId.
To get baseId, use the search_bases or list_bases tool.

cursor.description:
The cursor to start from. To begin from the first record, do not include a cursor.
For a subsequent paginated request, include the nextCursor from the previous response.

operands.description:
The operands (arguments) to the comparison operator.
The first operand must be a field ID. Example: "fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM". Do not substitute user-facing names for IDs.
The second operand depends on the operator and field type:
    - isEmpty, isNotEmpty: No second operand (use a single-element array with just the field ID).
    - =, !=, contains, doesNotContain: A string for text fields, a number for number fields, a boolean for checkbox fields.
    - <, >, <=, >=: A number.
    - For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields: The second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selABCDEFGHIJKLM") obtained from get_table_schema, not the choice
    name.
    - hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, doesNotContain: An array of strings (e.g., choice IDs for select fields, collaborator IDs for collaborator fields).
    - For date/datetime fields with =, !=, <, >, <=, >=: The second operand is a date value object, e.g. {"mode": "today", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "exactDate",
    "exactDate": "2024-01-15", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, or {"mode": "daysAgo", "numberOfDays": 7, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - isWithin (date fields only): The second operand is a date range object, e.g. {"mode": "pastWeek", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}, {"mode": "pastNumberOfDays", "numberOfDays":
    30, "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.
    - filename: A string to match against attachment filenames.
    - fileType: Either "image" or "text".
For singleSelect/multipleSelects fields, the second operand must be a choice ID (e.g., "selet1KAKDTOhXQJk") obtained from get_table_schema.

operator.description:
The comparison operator for this filter condition, applied to the operands.
Acceptable values are =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, isWithin, isAnyOf, isNoneOf, contains, doesNotContain, filename, fileType, isEmpty, isNotEmpty.
For singleSelect and singleCollaborator fields, use =, !=, isAnyOf, or isNoneOf.
For multipleSelects and multipleCollaborators fields, use hasAnyOf, hasAllOf, =, or doesNotContain.

matchGroupsByMembership.description:
Only set this when operand is a collaborator field.
When true, groups are matched by their individual members.
When false, groups are matched by their literal group ID.

operands.description:
A list of filter conditions to apply to the records. These are combined using the top-level operator (default "and").
Each filter condition must have an "operator" key (the comparison operator, e.g. "=", "contains", "isEmpty", etc) and an "operands" key (an array where
the first element is a field ID and the optional second element is the value to compare against).
Example: [{"operator": "contains", "operands": ["fld9x4rqyBSCLzsJM", "apple"]}]

operator.description:
The operator to use to combine the operands (filter conditions).
Acceptable values are 'and' and 'or'.
The default operator is 'and'.

tableId.description:

To discover tables, use the list_tables_for_base tool.

Pass in only the fields most useful for the user to see.
If not provided, all fields will be included in the result.
